Diz eklemini oluşturan diğer kemik yapıların korteks bütünlüğü, sinyal intensiteleri doğaldır.Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir.Ön çapraz bağ, lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir.Anterior çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyonu düşündürür sinyal değişiklikleri mevcuttur. Lateral menisküs sinyal intensitesi ve bütünlüğü doğaldır. Medial menisküs posterior hornunda kompleks yırtık ve eklem mesafesi dışına ekstrüzyon, hacim kaybı mevcuttur.  Bu düzeyde eklem mesafesinde daralma dikkati çekmiştir. Patellaposteriorunda kıkırdak dokuda incelme izlenmiştir (patellar kondromalazi).Popliteal fossada yer işgal eden lezyon saptanmadı.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Ongoing and worsening left knee pain, with popping, freezing, and knee pain.

COMPARISON:  Knee radiograph dated [Date].

FINDINGS:

Intrasubstance degeneration involving the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The anterior horn of the medial meniscus and the lateral meniscus are unremarkable.

ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Scattered areas of chondrosis with no significant fissuring or full thickness cartilage loss.

No joint effusion.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are unremarkable.

No evidence of bone marrow edema, fractures or dislocation.

0.5 cm popliteal cyst.


INTERPRETATION:

No evidence of meniscal tear or ligamentous injury.

MRI RIGHT KNEE

INDICATION: Very active, grinding pain recognized involving right knee worse when supine

Routine MRI of the right knee shows an oblique tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface. No lateral meniscal tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Extensor mechanism intact. Collateral ligaments are intact.

Small amount of joint fluid but no frank effusion. No baker's cyst. Mild prepatellar bursitis. The medial compartment shows moderate cartilage loss and tiny medial compartment osteophytes. Tiny degenerative cysts at the base of the medial tibial spine. Lateral compartment shows no cartilage defects. Severe cartilage loss along the width of the patella with 6 mm focus of bony edema at the patellar apex. 4 mm degenerative cyst at the medial trochlea.

IMPRESSION:

Oblique tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface.

Moderate cartilage loss medial femoral condyle.

Focal severe osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint with slight subchondral edema on both sides of the joint.
